text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said in Parliament yesterday that he is prepared to appear before the parliamentary commission probing the Tocsik affair, if asked, adding that the Socialist Party is not implicated in the case.
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman is planning to visit Hungary in April, the Zagreb daily Vjesnik reported.
- The police forces will receive an average 17 percent salary increase, retroactive to January 1.
- The Hungarian government must decide soon on its financial participation in infrastructure developments, said Eva Ehrlich of the Strategic Workgroup for European Integration.

- Union workers at the Husipari meat company in Szekszard are organising a demonstration outside Parliament next Monday against the German owner of the company, Gunther Schlegel, who they claim is ignoring workers' rights and fails to honour provisions in the privatisation contract.
NEPSZAVA

- Marta Tocsik, whose HUF 804 million consultancy fee has unleashed a political scandal, hit back in an extensive interview. Speaking about her negotiations with local governments said "I have equally held negotiations with the local government run by Smallholders, the Democratic Forum, the Young Democrats, the People's Party, the Christian Democrats, the Socialists and the Free Democrats.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Agriculture Ministry has imposed a ban on hunting wild game until March 1, when the new hunting law takes effect.
- A table summarizes parliamentary parties' finances.
- The procurement index stood at 45 in January, slightly higher than in the previous month.
- The leaders of the capital's luxury Marriott hotel have chosen Millenium Court as the name of their new facility in downtown Budapest.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Foreign Ministry state secretaries from Italy, Slovenia and Hungary are expected to meet in Rome this week.
- A 28-year-old Lithuanian man won $168,000 on Saturday in the biggest slot machine payoff in history of Hungarian casinos. The man put $3 into the machine.
- Customs guards caught a Nigerian man attempting to smuggle HUF 5 million worth of heroin. A medical examination showed that he had concealed heroin capsules in his stomach.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Some 40 million visitors came to Hungary last year, 2 percent more than in 1995.
- The total value of ongoing and planned investments in the construction industry came to HUF 400-500 billion last year, the sector's information firm Bau-Data reports.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- More than 150 local governments in southwest Hungary will sell off 37.22 percent of shares in the regional gas distributor Ddgaz late this month.
- Magyar Hitel Bank boosted its pre-tax profit by 245 percent to HUF 5.8 billion last year, according to preliminary figures.
- The equity of ball-bearing manufacturer Magyar Gordulocsapagy Muvek Rt. will be increased by HUF 500 million to HUF 5 billion by its South Korean owner Daewoo on February 21.
- A new open-ended investment fund, named Korinthos, will shortly be launched by the fund manager Obuda Alapkezelo.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
